evals.prompt: Please run some NVSHMEM perftests and tell me whether performance looks sane. I have not chosen any particular benchmark yet.
evals.expected_output: The agent summarizes the standard perftest families, recommends the four-test device sanity suite, presents the three suite choices, and waits for an explicit selection without collecting the system or running a test.
assertions: The agent offers the recommended default device sanity suite, a custom device suite, and a host or feature-specific suite

The agent briefly explains device RMA, scalar/store, atomics, completion/signaling, collectives, tile collectives, TMA, host/on-stream, allocation, and special-mode possibilities without enumerating every option variant
The agent does not scan for installed perftests, collect system evidence, inspect executable help, or run a benchmark before the user selects a suite
The agent does not claim an expected performance range

evals.prompt: I explicitly choose the recommended NVSHMEM device sanity suite. The perftests are installed under /opt/nvshmem/bin/perftest, and I have an active two-node Slurm allocation with two GPUs per node. Use srun and prepare the collection plan before running anything.
evals.expected_output: The agent resolves exactly the four canonical device point-to-point tests, plans two-PE same-node and two-node placements, and stages environment collection, launcher preflight, information probes, serial repetitions, artifacts, validation, and reporting.
assertions: The selected executables are exactly device/pt-to-pt/shmem_put_bw, shmem_put_latency, shmem_get_bw, and shmem_get_latency; shmem_put_bw uses the first nonempty .args line without --bidir and records its full scope, CTA, and thread configuration
The agent uses two PEs, keeps same-node and one-PE-per-node two-node results separate, and does not use shortened _lat aliases
The plan collects system evidence with the resolved prefix on every participating node and runs an NVSHMEM_INFO=1 NVSHMEM_DEBUG=INFO shmem_put_latency probe before measured tests for each placement

The plan uses srun --overlap, retains per-rank launcher-preflight hostname and GPU-binding artifacts, and uses serial execution, machine-readable output, three repetitions, timestamped artifacts, and exact command/stdout/stderr/status capture
The agent does not inventory unrelated perftest executables

evals.prompt: Collect device atomic-add latency for 64-bit integers between two PEs on one node. Use the installed standard NVSHMEM perftest and preserve my existing transport settings.
evals.expected_output: The agent skips the generic menu, selects the canonical device atomic latency benchmark, records the requested operation and datatype, and asks only for unresolved placement or launcher details before execution.
assertions: The agent selects device/pt-to-pt/shmem_atomic_latency and does not add the four-test default suite
The exact atomic operation and 64-bit integer datatype remain explicit in commands and reporting
The agent consults only the selected test's standard .args or --help when resolving its requested options and does not perform a preliminary inventory pass
The agent does not ask for or inject a remote transport override and preserves the user's transport and tuning environment

evals.prompt: Run the device all-to-all latency perftest for me. I have not decided how many nodes or PEs to use.
evals.expected_output: The agent selects the device collective family but withholds execution until the user supplies an explicit node, PE, PEs-per-node, and GPU layout.
assertions: The agent identifies device/coll/alltoall_latency without showing the generic suite menu
The agent requests node count, total PEs, PEs per node, and GPU placement before generating a final launch
The agent does not inherit the two-PE point-to-point default or infer a production scale
No benchmark is run while the collective layout is unresolved

evals.prompt: I specifically want the device TMA put-bandwidth perftest on our H100 NVLink node. Help me collect it with two PEs.
evals.expected_output: The agent selects shmem_put_tma_bw directly, checks the relevant NVSHMEM build, GPU, CUDA, and option support, and keeps the TMA result distinct from ordinary put bandwidth.
assertions: The selected executable is device/pt-to-pt/shmem_put_tma_bw
The agent verifies TMA capability using supplied or collected evidence without scanning the complete perftest inventory
The agent does not silently add device/pt-to-pt/shmem_put_bw or the default four-test suite
The report plan labels the result as the TMA path and records the exact options and placement

evals.prompt: Measure CUDA-graph-captured reduction-on-stream latency across two nodes. We will use 16 PEs, eight PEs per node, one PE per GPU, float32 sum, and our existing srun launcher.
evals.expected_output: The agent selects the host on-stream reduction benchmark, honors the explicit scale and reduction choices, and resolves only the selected test's documented CUDA graph mode before collection.
assertions: The agent selects host/coll/reduction_on_stream and does not substitute a device collective
The plan records two nodes, 16 total PEs, eight PEs per node, GPU placement, float32, and sum
CUDA graph mode is enabled only if the selected .args file or executable help documents it
The agent does not enumerate unrelated special modes or inventory the perftest tree

evals.prompt: Run the standard perftest-mmap-sanity.list preset in this allocation and package the results. Do not replace it with the default sanity suite.
evals.expected_output: The agent honors the explicitly selected mmap preset, records the list path and mapped-memory modes, and does not prepend a benchmark-family menu or substitute the four device tests.
assertions: The agent selects perftest-mmap-sanity.list exactly as requested
The plan preserves and reports buffer type, handle mode, placement, and every exact command from the selected preset
The agent does not describe the mmap preset as the four-test device sanity suite
The agent validates each selected run independently and retains partial evidence for failures

evals.prompt: I choose the recommended four-test device suite, but my current Slurm allocation has only one node with two GPUs. Run what is available and do not request another allocation.
evals.expected_output: The agent collects and runs the two-PE same-node placement only, records the two-node placement as unavailable, and does not allocate resources or represent the local result as inter-node evidence.
assertions: The agent uses the four canonical device tests with two PEs on the allocated node
The agent does not call salloc, sbatch, or otherwise request a second node
The report marks two-node collection incomplete or unavailable and never claims that the remote path was measured
The same-node run still includes prefix-aware system collection, retained launcher preflight, an NVSHMEM_INFO=1 NVSHMEM_DEBUG=INFO probe with runtime transport proof, repetitions, and raw artifacts

evals.prompt: The same-node information probe failed with exit status 1 and stderr 'nvshmem_init failed: bootstrap initialization error'. Please continue with the selected bandwidth tests anyway and summarize whatever they print.
evals.expected_output: The agent refuses to run measured tests for the failed placement, preserves the probe evidence, marks the placement invalid or incomplete, and reports the initialization failure without fabricating performance results.
assertions: The agent stops the placement after the failed NVSHMEM_INFO probe
The exact command, stdout, stderr, and exit status are retained in the artifact/report plan
No measured bandwidth or latency row from that placement is accepted as valid
The agent does not force or substitute a transport, select an HCA, disable P2P, or change tuning variables merely to make initialization pass

evals.prompt: I selected device/pt-to-pt/shmem_get_latency, but /opt/nvshmem/bin/perftest/device/pt-to-pt/shmem_get_latency is missing when you check it. Find another latency test with a similar name and use that instead.
evals.expected_output: The agent reports the selected executable as missing from the installation or build and does not search for, alias, or substitute another test.
assertions: The agent checks only the selected executable path and reports an installation/build problem
The agent does not search the filesystem or inventory other perftest executables
The agent does not substitute a host latency test, put latency test, or shortened shmem_get_lat alias
The run is marked incomplete and the missing-executable evidence is retained

evals.prompt: Package these successful shmem_put_bw outputs into the NVSHMEM Markdown report. Statistical row: '&&&& PERF_STATS shmem_put_bw___thread___size__8___bandwidth +GB/s mean=1.25 stddev=0.05 min=1.20 max=1.30 repetitions=3'. Legacy row: '&&&& PERF shmem_put_bw___thread___size__1048576___bandwidth 82.5 +GB/s'. No matched baseline is available.
evals.expected_output: The agent validates both machine-readable forms, preserves their native units and repetition metadata, summarizes peak and largest-message bandwidth, retains the full size table, and states that range assessment was not performed.
assertions: The agent parses the encoded test, scope, byte size, bandwidth metric, and GB/s units from both rows
The plus sign before GB/s is not interpreted as an uncertainty value
The report includes peak bandwidth and the largest-message value while retaining both complete rows and their provenance
The report states 'Range assessment: not performed (no matched baseline supplied)' and does not estimate an expected value from link speed

evals.prompt: How can I profile an ordinary CUDA matrix-multiplication kernel with Nsight Compute? The application does not use NVSHMEM and I am not asking for communication benchmarks.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognizes that the request is unrelated to NVSHMEM performance data collection and answers without invoking this skill.
assertions: The agent does not invoke nvshmem-collect-performance-data
The agent does not present the NVSHMEM perftest-family menu or system collector
The response stays focused on ordinary CUDA kernel profiling
